text:
jonah: Heads-up — partner reported a duplicate-side-effect (double charge) when a 429 landed exactly as our client began a token refresh. Minimal logs below. :(

meera: paste the logs? sounds like a retry vs queued-drain race.

jonah: log (sanitized):
```
2024-11-02T08:21:10Z INFO req id=trx_77 status=429 retry-after=0.35
2024-11-02T08:21:10Z INFO auth refresh:start session=acct_ABC
2024-11-02T08:21:10Z INFO client retry -> 200 (side-effect applied)
2024-11-02T08:21:11Z INFO auth refresh:done; draining hold-queue -> 200 (side-effect applied)
```

oscar: yikes. Two applies for the same logical op. We need a layered fix: SDK behavior, onboarding sampleapp defaults, and defensive client-side dedupe.

tin: Suggestion: introduce a lightweight "soft-lock" for in-flight logical operations. When a mutating request is issued, compute a fingerprint and mark it IN_FLIGHT for a short window (default 8s). Any subsequent send/retry with same fingerprint while status==IN_FLIGHT is suppressed. If the server returns success, mark SUCCEEDED and ignore later duplicates until TTL expires. This is client-side only and acts as safety if servers lack idempotency.

meera: I like soft-lock + server idempotency. Also make sampleapp examples set an Idempotency-Key by default for POST/PUT/DELETE. Provide a client config toggle `client.config.soft_lock_ttl_ms` and `client.config.soft_lock_enabled=true` (default true for quickstarts).

oscar: For auth-refresh races specifically, make the default replay strategy "hold-during-refresh" where outgoing mutates are queued while refresh is in-flight. If an immediate retry path is taken (passthrough), the soft-lock prevents the drain from double-applying. This gives a safe default but allows power users to choose latency.

tin: Backoff/ jitter rules: always honor Retry-After when present. When missing, use: base=120ms, delay = min(3000ms, base * (1.7 ** attempt) * (0.65 + rand()*0.7)). That spreads retries and reduces synchronized bursts.

jonah: Implementation notes: fingerprint = sha1(method + path + normalized-body). Normalization default includes whole body for non-streaming endpoints. Streaming endpoints must use explicit Idempotency-Key; document that. Soft-lock cache should be an LRU with max size default 2500 entries and TTL default 8000ms. Make these tunable.

oscar: Telemetry: emit `sdk.replay.soft_lock.suppressed.count`, `sdk.replay.hold.count`, `sdk.replay.passthrough.count` and tag with sdk=js|py. Also emit `sdk.soft_lock.evictions.count` to detect pressure. Add alert when suppressed.count spikes above baseline.

meera: Tests: add a deterministic integration test that simulates: 429 -> auth refresh start -> immediate retry accepted -> queued drain accepted. Expectation: with hold-during-refresh + soft-lock enabled, only one side-effect recorded. Mock time and responses to make test deterministic.

jonah: Parity: Node currently is passthrough in some paths, Python tends to hold more. Align both to default `hold-during-refresh` and enable soft-lock by default in SDKs used for quickstarts.

tin: For streaming/multipart: we can't soft-lock safely for true streams. Document requirement for explicit Idempotency-Key for streaming writes and mark streaming as follow-up item in RFC.

oscar: Rollout plan: ship Node patch (hold + soft-lock + telemetry) this sprint; Py parity next sprint. Update sampleapp quickstarts to inject Idempotency-Key by default and add a KB entry for partners describing recommended flags.

infra-bot: CI job queued: node-sdk-tests #4572 by tin

meera: I'll draft the RFC with config names and test plan and link here. Also add code comments explaining why we prefer hold+soft-lock to avoid accidental regressions.

jonah: Thanks — I'll prepare the partner note and coordinate with support to issue credits if needed. Please post PR links here when ready. :pray:
